title: The Green Journal of Hesper
law: The farm's plant speaks: not with a voice, but through leaves, which twist into signs that children read better than old people. Whatever the plant asks is granted: if it wants warmer water the whole farm warms; if it wants blood, someone cuts his hand over the roots and is not bandaged until the plant stops shaking. Requests are written in the green journal, and anyone who fails them within three days wakes without a tooth, then without a finger, then without an eye; no one has ever reached the fourth day. The plant may not know about other plants, so stories of forests and fields are forbidden, and those who tell them are set to work in silence at the roots. Once every nine years the plant flowers and then asks for a new name: the crew gives it the name of a dead child, and that child is never mentioned again on the farm, so as not to offend the flower.
premise: The plant asks for blood for the third day running, and the doctor is arguing with the officer over who cuts, because the crew's arms are covered in scars.
summary: On the orbital farm Hesper the only plant speaks through the shapes its leaves make, and every request it writes into the green journal must be carried out within three days or the crew member who failed it wakes without a tooth, then without a finger, then without an eye.
